Chat with your docs. Automate complex workflows with AI Agents. Hyper-configurable, multi-user ready, battle-tested—and runs locally by default with zero setup friction. ![Chatting](https://github.com/Mintplex-Labs/anything-llm/releases/download/v1.11.2/AnythingLLM720p.gif)

### Product Overview AnythingLLM is the all-in-one AI application that lets you build a private, fully-featured ChatGPT—without compromises. Connect your favorite local or cloud LLM, ingest your documents, and start chatting in minutes. Out of the box you get built-in agents, multi-user support, vector databases, and document pipelines — no extra configuration required. AnythingLLM supports multiple users as well where you can control the access and experience per user without compromising the security or privacy of the instance or your intellectual property. ## Cool Features of AnythingLLM - [Dynamic Model Routing](https://docs.anythingllm.com/model-router/overview) - Automatically route chats to the best provider & model for the conversation based on rules you define. - [Automatic & User Managed Memories](https://docs.anythingllm.com/features/memories) - Have your LLM remember important information about you or your workspace. - [Scheduled Tasks](https://docs.anythingllm.com/scheduled-jobs/overview) - Run recurring tasks or prompts on a cron schedule with full agent capabilities. - [Intelligent Skill Selection](https://docs.anythingllm.com/agent/intelligent-tool-selection) Enable **unlimited** tools for your models while reducing token usage by up to 80% per query - [No-code AI Agent builder](https://docs.anythingllm.com/agent-flows/overview) - [MCP-compatibility](https://docs.anythingllm.com/mcp-compatibility/overview) - [Multi-modal support (both closed and open-source LLMs!)](https://docs.anythingllm.com/features/language-models) - [Custom AI Agents](https://docs.anythingllm.com/agent/custom/introduction) - 👤 Multi-user instance support and permissioning _Docker version only_ - 🦾 Agents inside your workspace (browse the web, etc) - 💬 [Custom Embeddable Chat widget for your website](https://github.com/Mintplex-Labs/anyt

profile.one_liner: AnythingLLM is a self-hostable chat app where teams or individuals talk to their own documents with any cloud or local model, and can run AI agents that browse the web, use tools and run scheduled tasks.
stack: JavaScript (Node/Express server and collector, React + Vite frontend)
openai SDK, @anthropic-ai/sdk, ollama (many providers through one interface)
LanceDB by default, plus Pinecone, Chroma, Qdrant, Weaviate, Milvus, PGVector

jobs.job: Chat with the many model providers behind one interface
jobs.how: A provider class per vendor wraps its SDK. Anthropic uses @anthropic-ai/sdk with optional prompt caching. Many others reuse the openai client. Attachments are turned into message content.

The default is a local ONNX model, Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, run through transformers.js. Other local models and many hosted embedding APIs can be chosen instead. Vectors are stored in LanceDB or another vector database.
An optional local cross-encoder, Xenova/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2, rescores retrieved chunks on CPU in small batches. It works only with some vector databases.

jobs.job: Run agents that call tools, including MCP servers
jobs.how: A home-built agent framework called AIbitat runs the conversation loop and tool calls, with a tool reranker to pick skills. MCP servers are booted, their tools listed, and each is turned into an agent plugin. Agent flows are no-code step lists stored as files.

jobs.job: Search the web for the agent
jobs.how: The web-browsing skill sends queries to search engine APIs (a Google-style engine is shown) and passes titles, links, snippets and answer boxes back to the model.

jobs.job: Route each chat to a chosen model
jobs.how: Users define routers with rules and a fallback provider and model, plus a cooldown. A rule can use an LLM to classify the message from a description.

jobs.job: Transcribe audio and video, and speak replies
jobs.how: The collector uses OpenAI whisper-1 or a built-in local transcriber. The server can use OpenAI speech-to-text, and text-to-speech goes through OpenAI, ElevenLabs, Piper in the browser, or the browser itself.

jobs.job: Expose workspaces as an OpenAI-style API
jobs.how: The server offers /v1/openai endpoints where each workspace shows up as a model, and it supports streaming. Other apps can call it with the normal OpenAI client.

stack_lock: Node.js app: libraries must be npm packages, and new local models must be ONNX or transformers.js weights (Xenova-style) to run in-process
Any model that runs in a separate server (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp-compatible) can be added as another provider if it speaks an OpenAI-style API
Vector stores, rerankers and embedders can be swapped one by one through the existing provider folders
New agent abilities can come in as MCP servers, agent flows or custom plugins without changing the code
Python-only libraries can be used only behind an HTTP service or an MCP server
Code is JavaScript: only libraries in JavaScript, unless they ship an MCP server or an API.
Local models: only ONNX or transformers.js weights.
APIs, MCP servers and skills always pass.

findings.title: Google has shut down gemini-2.0-flash-lite
findings.why: gemini-2.0-flash-lite was shut down on 1 Jun 2026. Announced on 18 Feb 2026. Named successor: gemini-3.5-flash or gemini-3.1-flash-lite. The default Gemini model in settings, the provider class and the agent provider is still the retired lite model, so anyone on the default gets failed requests. Change the default to gemini-3.1-flash-lite, the successor the lever names, in all three places.

findings.why: The web-browsing skill only reads Google-style search results (titles, links, snippets, answer boxes) from search engine APIs. Exa's official MCP server says it offers web search, content fetching and multi-step research, so the agent could also read full pages and research across steps. AnythingLLM already runs MCP servers and turns their tools into agent plugins, so you only add it in MCP settings. There is no independent comparison with the current search.

findings.title: Three default model ids sent to OpenAI and Google are shut down or about to be, so those requests will fail
findings.why: These are the models a fresh install uses when the user has not picked one. OpenAI says gpt-4.1-nano is shut down (23 Oct 2026) and gpt-4o shuts down on 14 Jan 2027. Google says gemini-2.0-flash-lite was shut down on 1 Jun 2026. Change each default to the successor the vendor names. Run your tests, because the newer models reject some parameters such as temperature, and the successors cost more or less depending on the model.

findings.title: Cut the cost and delay of routing each chat by using a purpose-built decision call instead of a full agent run

where.text: You are a message classifier for a model router.

findings.why: When a router rule uses an LLM, classifyWithLLM starts a whole headless agent on the router's fallback model just to pick one category from the admin's rule list. That list is fixed before the call, so it is a plain label pick. A decision endpoint could do it, with a confidence threshold, and the current agent call kept as the fallback below the threshold. This means adding a new call path in classifyWithLLM and tuning a threshold on your own rules. Neither vendor has been compared with the model you use today.

options.name: TypeSafe Jev
options.what: TypeSafe says responses take 70ms-500ms, "40x-200x faster" than frontier models on these queries; there is no independent study. It costs $0.042 per 1M input tokens, with output tokens free. English is where accuracy is best, so test other languages on your own rules first.
options.needs: A TypeSafe key, a call to POST /v1/systemone with a Choice question, and a confidence gate with today's call as the fallback.

options.name: OpenAI Decisions API
options.what: OpenAI says typed answers are "about 10x faster than the Responses API"; nobody has measured it on this code. It costs $0.10 per 1M uncached input tokens on gpt-6-luna, and output tokens are not charged. It supports only gpt-6-luna, so it ties this call to OpenAI.
options.needs: An OpenAI key, a call to POST /v1/decisions with a choice question and an "other" fallback option, and a threshold set from labeled examples.

findings.title: OpenAI's whisper-1 shuts down on 26 Feb 2027

where.text: "No OpenAI compatible STT model was set. We will use the default model 'whisper-1'. This may not exist or be valid for your selected endpoint."

findings.why: whisper-1 shuts down on 26 Feb 2027. Announced on 26 Aug 2026. Named successor: gpt-live-transcribe or gpt-transcribe. The collector, the server speech-to-text providers and the settings pickers send whisper-1 to OpenAI, so transcription will fail after the shutdown. Switch the defaults to gpt-transcribe and retest your audio; the generic and Lemonade providers only matter if the endpoint behind them stops offering whisper-1.

options.name: OpenAI whisper-1 shuts down on 26 Feb 2027; move to gpt-transcribe
options.what: For recorded audio, change whisper-1 to gpt-transcribe on /v1/audio/transcriptions. For live audio, use gpt-live-transcribe. Test with audio like yours: accents, noise, names and numbers.
options.needs: Nothing new; the same OpenAI key.

evidence: Announced the deprecation of whisper-1 , gpt-4o-transcribe , gpt-4o-mini-transcribe , and gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize .

findings.title: @xenova/transformers has had no release since 29 May 2024
findings.why: collector/package.json:20 and server/package.json:41 declare ^2.14.0, released 10 Jan 2024. The latest is 2.17.2, released 29 May 2024. Local embeddings, reranking and the built-in transcriber all run on this library, and it has had no release for a long time. It still works today, so plan a move to a maintained fork rather than a rushed change.

findings.title: Let users add agent skills published in the open SKILL.md format, not just AnythingLLM's own plugin folders
findings.why: Imported agent skills load only from a plugins/agent-skills folder, each with its own handler.js that the server requires directly, so folders with a SKILL.md can't be used. Adding a loader that reads a SKILL.md folder's name and description at start and its full instructions on demand would let users bring skills published elsewhere. Skills can bundle scripts, so they need the same path checks the current imports get, and the old format has to keep working alongside the new one.
